proof.text: Apply the polynomial base-change concentration theorem: Koszul regularity makes the quotient cotangent complex both at least and at most degree −1. This uses the original polynomial Koszul resolution, Tor-independent cotangent base change, and free polynomial augmentation conormal calculation.

Independently, apply the general quotient conormal homology theorem to I=(f). It identifies H⁻¹ of the standard differential complex with I/I² and carries every displayed standard relation cycle to a mod I².

Use the localization/homology comparison to obtain the prescribed H⁻¹ isomorphism from L to I/I². An object concentrated in one degree is isomorphic to a single object. Correct such an isomorphism by the single of its H⁻¹ automorphism so that its induced homology map is exactly the prescribed one. Composing with the concrete-complex homology comparison then gives the required normalization on every relation cycle.
For i≠−1, either i<−1 or i>−1. The two t-structure bounds give IsZero Hⁱ(L) in the respective cases. All steps are valid for the empty sequence, the unit ideal, and the zero ring.

title: Full cotangent complex of a Koszul-regular quotient
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $r\geq0$, and $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in R$ a Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Put $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ and $B=R/I$. For the standard cotangent complex [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] in $D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the canonical conormal identification induces an isomorphism $L_{B/R}\simeq(I/I^2)[1]$. Thus $H^i(L_{B/R})=0$ for every $i\ne-1$, with no Noetherian hypothesis.
